column5: created and formed Israel, called by name
column6: The commentary says the Lord is identified by deeds rather than a remote epithet; Isaiah names YHWH as the one who created and formed Jacob, redeemed him and called him by name.

column5: created and formed for God's glory
column6: The commentary ties glorifying the Lord's Name to the works that identify him; Isaiah says the people called by God's name were created and formed for his glory.

column5: formed Israel from the womb
column6: The commentary develops bodily formation in the womb as a secondary sense alongside creation; Isaiah names YHWH as the one who made and formed Jacob from the womb and will help him.

column5: Hebrew שוה, leveling a field before sowing
column6: The source commentary explicitly labels سوى with straightening and balance; Isaiah uses Hebrew שוה for leveling a field's surface before seed is sown, a close cognate use in an agricultural setting that does not determine the Qur'anic verb's full sense.

column5: hands make and fashion, then grant understanding
column6: The commentary joins being made to the guidance that follows; the psalmist says God's hands made and fashioned him, then asks for understanding to learn God's commands.

column5: Spirit leads the speaker on level ground
column6: The commentary connects proportioning, guidance and the straight path; the psalm asks God to teach his will and let his good Spirit lead the speaker on level ground.

column5: life and breath of every creature in God's hand
column6: The commentary treats each body as evidence of its Maker and develops breath as the completion of form; Job says the life of every creature and breath of humankind are in God's hand.

column5: God's Spirit makes and breath gives life
column6: The commentary connects bodily formation to life-giving breath; Job says the Spirit of God made him and the breath of the Almighty gives him life.

column5: life, care and steadfast love preserve the spirit
column6: The commentary says the formed body bears the trace of the Lord's work; Job adds that the same God who formed him granted life and care that preserved his spirit.

column5: created humans receive a task and blessing
column6: The commentary links creation to the suitable direction that follows; after creating male and female, Genesis blesses them and gives them a role toward the other creatures.

column5: idols are nothing, YHWH made the heavens
column6: The commentary contrasts the Creator with things fabricated for worship; the psalm calls the nations' gods idols and says YHWH made the heavens.

column5: worship before YHWH the Maker
column6: The commentary ties glorification to the Creator's acts; the psalm calls the congregation to bow before YHWH because he is their Maker.

column5: blessing for the body's openings and functions
column6: The commentary asks the hearer to recognize the Creator in the body's fitted parts; this rabbinic blessing thanks God for forming the human body with its openings and cavities, whose obstruction would prevent life.

column5: the Maker forms, inspires soul and breathes life
column6: The commentary contrasts the living Creator with lifeless images made by artisans; Wisdom says the idol-maker failed to know the one who formed him, inspired an active soul and breathed a living spirit into him.

column5: Solomon molded in the womb like every human
column6: The commentary develops bodily formation before birth and the common human process; Solomon says he too was molded in flesh in his mother's womb and received breath like all people.

column5: humans made in God's image
column6: The commentary reads creation as including the listener's own body; Ben Sira says God endowed humans with strength and made them in his image.

column5: eyes, ears and a thinking heart
column6: The commentary extends proportioned creation to inward and sensory capacities; Ben Sira says God gave humans discernment, eyes, ears and a heart for thinking.

column5: knowledge of good and evil
column6: The commentary links making with subsequent moral direction; Ben Sira says God filled humanity with knowledge and understanding and showed them good and evil.

column5: rewritten scroll includes all former words and more
column6: The commentary sets the secondary image of omitting a letter beside the promise of preserved recitation; after the king burns the scroll, Jeremiah dictates it again with all its former words and many more.

column5: water wears stone and washes soil away
column6: The commentary describes smoothness as wear that flattens a surface; Job says waters wear stones and torrents wash away the soil, giving a direct image of erosion.

column5: Tyre's walls reduced to bare rock
column6: The commentary connects the smooth rock with a settlement leveled to the ground; Ezekiel's oracle says Tyre's walls and towers will be broken, its dust scraped away and the site left like bare rock.

column5: Zion plowed like a field and Jerusalem made ruins
column6: The commentary links سوى's leveling sense to the end of a created settlement; Micah warns that Zion will be plowed like a field and Jerusalem become a heap of ruins because of its rulers' injustice.

column5: woman from man, man through woman, all from God
column6: The commentary describes parts as fitted in relation and notes created pairs; Paul recalls the creation relation between man and woman but concludes that all things are from God.

column5: all things hold together in Christ
column6: The commentary's سوى emphasizes that a whole is made complete through relations among its parts; Colossians says all things hold together in Christ, extending that order to the cosmos.

column5: every hair on the disciples' heads is numbered
column6: The commentary says the listener can find the Creator's work in the body; in a teaching about the Father's care, Jesus says even the hairs of the disciples' heads are numbered.

column5: rain, fruitful seasons and food as witness
column6: The commentary follows creation into pasture and provision for people and animals; Paul says God gives rain, fruitful seasons and food, leaving a witness of his goodness.

column5: man and woman are not independent in the Lord
column6: The commentary describes proportion as relation rather than mere leveling; Paul says woman and man are not independent of one another in the Lord, giving paired creation a mutual reading.

column5: outer person decays while inner person renews
column6: The commentary develops the worn garment and the reversal of bodily order with age; Paul says the outer person is wasting away while the inner person is renewed day by day.

column5: spirit, soul and body kept complete
column6: The commentary treats fitting form as extending through body and inward life; Paul prays that the whole spirit, soul and body be kept blameless, an explicit Christian formula of integrated completeness.

column5: moon and sun assigned their times
column6: The commentary treats the moon's gradual fullness as completion and cites its phases as measured; the psalm says God appointed the moon for seasons and the sun knows its setting.

column5: all works made in wisdom
column6: The commentary presents the created world as measured and complete; the psalm marvels at the many works of YHWH and says they were all made in wisdom.

column5: creatures wait for food from God
column6: The commentary describes pasture and crop as provision for living creatures; the psalm says all creatures look to God for their food in its season.

column5: God opens his hand and satisfies creatures
column6: The commentary says the created order is fitted to sustain people and animals; the psalm says God gives food when he opens his hand and satisfies every living thing.

column5: humanity made for incorruption in God's image
column6: The commentary connects created form with later bodily wearing and death; Wisdom says God made humans for incorruption and in the image of his own eternity, offering a Jewish account in which death is not the intended completion.

column5: creation includes the heavenly host
column6: The commentary says the ayah's objectless creation can encompass all things; Jubilees' creation account includes the heavens and their host, expanding the creation scene beyond the human body.
